title: Project debrief: what can explain the diesel crack, and how was it built?
rubric: States the research question and the answer so far: daily diesel-crack changes are mostly noise; yesterday's move (partial reversal) and the gap to the 60-day mean (mean reversion) are the only candidates with a stable sign; the crack level is strongly seasonal (winter ≈ 19.5 vs summer ≈ 14 USD/bbl).
Explains the unit work: all products in USD/bbl (×42 for gallons, ÷7.45 / ÷7.88 for tonnes) before any crack.
Explains the gap treatment by cause: leading and trailing gaps left missing, holidays carried ≤ 2 days and flagged, a frozen gasoil feed removed, one row per date enforced on the index.
Separates missing from zero in physical data (the August 2018 'collapse' was a non-report).
Separates errors from events with evidence: the RBOB ×10 print removed, the August 2017 outage kept and annotated; robust, past-only scores used to flag.
Defines the information set (morning of t, data to t−1), the shifts, and the truncation check.
Warns about the settlement-time lead between ULSD and gasoil, and lists limits: small correlations, synthetic data, thresholds as judgement calls, selection risk.
